title: Isomorphisms descend along etale surjections
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $u:U\to X$ be a surjective etale morphism of
separated finite-type
$k$-schemes, and let $\varphi:M\to N$ be a morphism of bounded
constructible complexes on $X$. If $Lu^*\varphi$ is an isomorphism,
then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: The singleton family indexed by Unit with arrow f is an etale cover by Surjective f and Etale f. Apply Scheme.ofArrows_mem_precoverage_iff and lem-pur-etale-proetale-cover (Scheme.etalePrecoverage_le_proetalePrecoverage) to obtain the pro-etale covering condition, including the empty-base case.

Use ProEtale.upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction from the published inverse-image construction to identify fixed-scalar inverse image with sectionwise localization restriction for the weakly etale map f. The published ProEtale.isIso_of_isIso_localizationRestriction applies to the singleton pro-etale cover: locally defined inverses agree on overlaps and glue by the sheaf axiom. NatIso.isIso_map_iff transports this detection through the comparison. Thus ProEtale.upperStar reflects isomorphisms of fixed-scalar module sheaves.

The finite coefficient inverse image sfIntrinsicPullback is, by definition, the conjugate of fixed-scalar upperStar through the canonical module realization equivalences. Equivalence functors reflect isomorphisms, so their composite with upperStar does too. This uses the actual finite-level functor defining def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom; no comparison with arbitrary pro-etale geometric stalks is involved.

For any derived morphism a whose sfIntrinsicDerivedPullback is invertible, each homology map of its image is invertible. The natural isomorphism (sfIntrinsicPullback A f).mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso n identifies it with sfIntrinsicPullback applied to H^n(a). This comparison is the published localization of lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology. Reflection at the sheaf level gives IsIso H^n(a) for every integer n. Apply DerivedCategory.isIso_iff, lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology, to obtain IsIso a.

Apply derived reflection to phi.hom using the stated pullback hypothesis. The intrinsic finite-torsion constructible category is a full subcategory, so its inclusion reflects isomorphisms and yields IsIso phi without changing any boundedness or constructibility assumption.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-Codex-Q33-c6f9a7524 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS for Q33/lem-pur-etale-iso-descent. The statement is unchanged and matches both blueprint snapshots exactly. Coefficients are A=A_{E,n} on X_proet (scope from def-pur-conventions), D^b_c is the full subcategory from def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, and Lu^* is the finite-level pullback from def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom. The stmt_deps changes are justified: smooth morphisms are dropped, and separated comes from def-weil-proper-morphism. The delivery has no new nodes, proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and the graph is acyclic. Step 1: étale implies weakly étale (det-pe (1), Stacks 094X(4)) and the map is open (UniversallyOpen.of_flat, 01UA); with quasi-compactness of V this is exactly the condition in Stacks 0989 (proetale.tex:2126). Step 2: I checked that the graph pair (W,γ) is initial in I_W, because pr_U∘φ is the structure map, so the colimit is F(W). Inverse image is therefore restriction, and that restriction is exact by lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact. Step 3: termwise representability is stated in the pullback definition, and homologyFunctorIso gives the natural comparison. Step 4 is an elementary sheaf-axiom gluing argument, complete and covering X=∅. Step 5: DerivedCategory.isIso_iff (HomologySequence.lean:88) plus fullness of D^b_c. The proof departs from the blueprint's geometric-stalk argument, and the departure is justified: lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative (4) shows stalk non-conservativity, and its cover-locality clause (1) is a generalization only in the different Λ_{T,Proet} category, so it is not cited and same_as stays []. I accept the three declared tool uses: det-pe-morphisms-etale-comparison, lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization and lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact. No SGA source is cited. No fixes were needed.
